feature_candidates.description: Per (user, video) counters: times seen in session/window, time since last exposure, dwell-time stats from train-only logs.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Captures re-impression patterns and recency effects that predict long_view re-engagement.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Add to src.models.features.history_features; compute from train-only sorted logs; no validation rowwise aggregates.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if computed strictly from train rows before the validation timestamp; avoid global day-level aggregates.
feature_candidates.name: User-item recency & re-impression count (history_features)

feature_candidates.description: Per video average long_view rate within tab and hour-bin, computed only from train data, smoothed with Laplace.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Provides stable item effect adjusted for tab context, improving discrimination within user impressions.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Precompute train-only statistics grouped by video, tab, hour bin; used as feature in model.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if computed from train only; watch for time-based leakage if aggregated over whole training period but not validation.
feature_candidates.name: Category/tab-conditional long_view propensity (item-side)

feature_candidates.description: User's click/like/comment rates in last 1h/24h from train-log history, normalized per user to encode propensity.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Captures short-term user engagement state that correlates with long_view, improving ranking.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Build rolling counters from train-only sequences; add to history_features and optionally as auxiliary targets.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Medium if computed across validation; must strictly use train-only temporal prefix.
feature_candidates.name: Session momentum counters (time-aware interaction rates)

findings.evidence: Train tab breakdown (DATA CARD) shows tab-specific long_view rates ranging 0.42%–61.25%.
findings.implication: Group-softmax or bpr models should score per (video, tab) or condition on tab; tab-conditional video quality may be a stronger signal than global video popularity.
findings.observation: Long_view rate varies strongly by tab (tab=4 48.93%, tab=1 38.61%, tab=0 4.22%), and tab shares differ within users, implying tab-conditional item effects matter.
findings.title: Tab dominates within-user variation

findings.evidence: Label rates from DATA CARD show distinct base rates and likely engagement hierarchy.
findings.implication: Multi-task auxiliary targets (click, like, comment) may stabilize long_view ranking, especially for sparse positive users, without leaking item-level periodic aggregates.
findings.observation: is_click rate (46.3%) is much higher than long_view (33.7%); like/comment/follow are rare (0.1–2.5%) but likely correlated with long_view.
findings.title: Cross-task labels co-occur and could regularize

findings.evidence: Measured Dead Ends in DATA CARD: first-order user-only terms contribute 0 to within-user ranking.
findings.implication: Feature engineering should focus on user-relative history (counts, recency) and item-side attributes, not static user profile fields.
findings.observation: Within-user ranking makes any user-constant feature contribute zero to order; measured dead end shows first-order user-only terms contribute exactly 0.
findings.title: User-static features add no ranking value

expected_artifacts: A markdown summary of within-user long_view rate vs. position, hourbin, and tab (train-only, with bootstrapped CIs).
A correlation heatmap of label co-occurrence and long_view, split by tab, to identify cross-task patterns.
A feature-importance ranking from a quick LightGBM run on train-only using a user-relative encoding (no global biases) to rank candidate features.
A proposal note listing 3–5 testable feature variants mapped to registered families and expected impact on GAUC/nDCG@5.
feature_hypotheses: Recent within-user exposure count and dwell-time statistics for the same video or category improve long_view prediction (history_features).
Time-aware interaction counters (e.g., clicks/likes in last 1h/24h) capture session momentum and can be added to bpr/group_softmax models.
Per-video quality proxies computed from train-only logs (not the leaky period table) such as average historical long_view rate conditional on tab yield a stable item effect.
Cross-task labels (is_click, is_like, is_comment) of the same impression can be used as auxiliary targets in a multi_task setting to regularize long_view ranking.
leakage_risks: The video statistics table is a full-platform period aggregate (90x larger than logged exposures) and must not be used unless explicitly caveated as leaky.
Any aggregate computed over the union of train and validation rows risks overfitting the validation labels for early stopping.
Time-based features computed across all users (e.g., global video popularity on a given day) may leak future information and break temporal split assumptions.
Including user-level static features in a within-user ranking model yields zero marginal contribution and may inflate computational cost without GAUC benefit.
plan.objective: Plan a leakage-safe EDA pass to uncover user- and item-side signals that improve within-user long_view ranking, targeting GAUC and nDCG@5 via registered families (bpr, group_softmax, history_features, multi_task).
questions: How does within-user long_view probability vary with position/recency and hourmin, especially controlling for tab?
Do repeated video impressions within a user show distinct long_view patterns (e.g., re-impression count, time since last impression)?
Are there stable user-level interaction propensities (click, like, comment) that predict long_view beyond the static profile?
Which video content attributes (category, upload_type, duration bin) show the largest within-user discrimination after removing tab effects?
required_inputs: Train and validation interaction logs with user_id, video_id, timestamp/hourmin, tab, and all binary labels.
Video metadata table (duration, category, upload_type, is_live_streamer) with coverage confirmed in train+valid.
User profile table (active_degree, follower_count, following_count, etc.) for user-side features.
Anonymized user historical interaction sequences (if available) for recency/count features.
